messages.author: 36cda290860fb7b2
messages.subject: Re: ChromosomeExplorer memory leaks
parts:
Hi All,

I am running 250K_Sty analysis of 28 samples against 48 HapMap
reference set. After performing all preprocessing steps I end up with
cesN containing 76 arrays.

Next, I do:

ces1<-extract(cesN,c(1:28));
ces2<-extract(cesN,c(29:76));
ceRef<-getAverageFile(ces2);
cbs<-CbsModel(ces1,cesRef);
fit(cbs,verbose=verbose);
ce<-ChromosomeExplorer(cbs);
setAlias(ce,"TEST");

everything fine at this point. But when I do:

ce<-process(ce,verbose=verbose),

the memory consumption grows
steadily from ~2GB to the upper memory limit of 32GB (this happens at the
array# ~ 15) and then the system crashes as expected.
I noticed the previous discussion on this subject in June but looks
like the issue was not resolved. There is also numerous discussions on
Cairo memory leaks with NVidia (that's what I have) elsewhere, so
probably this is a source of the problem.
Is there a workaround to fight this memory leak or should I generate
reports chunk by chunk of say 10 arrays?

Thank you,

Alex

thanks for reporting and troubleshooting this.

>> Hi All,
>>
>> I am running 250K_Sty analysis of 28 samples against 48 HapMap
>> reference set. After performing all preprocessing steps I end up with
>> cesN containing 76 arrays.
>>
>> Next, I do:
>>
>> ces1<-extract(cesN,c(1:28));
>> ces2<-extract(cesN,c(29:76));
>> ceRef<-getAverageFile(ces2);
>> cbs<-CbsModel(ces1,cesRef);
>> fit(cbs,verbose=verbose);
>> ce<-ChromosomeExplorer(cbs);
>> setAlias(ce,"TEST");
>>
>> everything fine at this point. But when I do:
>>
>> ce<-process(ce,verbose=verbose),
>>
>> the memory consumption grows
>> steadily from ~2GB to the upper memory limit of 32GB (this happens at the
>> array# ~ 15) and then the system crashes as expected.
>> I noticed the previous discussion on this subject in June but looks
>> like the issue was not resolved.

Could you please give the name of (and URL to) the thread you refer
to? If it is the one I guess it is, it should have been solved in the
latest update.

>> There is also numerous discussions on
>> Cairo memory leaks with NVidia (that's what I have) elsewhere, so
>> probably this is a source of the problem.
>> Is there a workaround to fight this memory leak or should I generate
>> reports chunk by chunk of say 10 arrays?

You say above that you have uninstalled Cairo; do you mean the 'Cairo'
package? Note that in R there is now a build in cairo device as well,
which is probably used in your case, because the package tries to
located a working PNG device in a given order. Internally, the PNG
device to be used to generate all graphs is found by:

pngDev <- findPngDevice(transparent=TRUE);

where findPngDevice() is an internal function located in aroma.core.
Have a look at the source code for this function in order to see which
and in what order PNG devices are scanned.

Since we're not using namespaces, you can easily override this
function to force the use of a specific PNG device, e.g.

findPngDevice <- function(transparent=TRUE, ...) {
if (transparent) function(...) png(..., bg=NA) else function(...) png(...);
}

See if you still have memory problems if you set another PNG (or JPG,
...) device like this. FYI, in R.utils there is also a png2() device
that utilizes the bitmap() device to generate PNGs.

I hope this helps you/us to identify the source of the memory issue,
so we can fix it/work around it. I'm not outruling there is something
funny going on in ChromosomeExplorer et al, but I hope not.

Cheers

Henrik

parts:
Hi Henrik,

I forced findPngDevice() to return png2: no memory leaks!

The default findPngDevice() returned:
function (...)
pngTyped(..., bg = NA, type = "cairo")
<environment: 0x17b59448>

So png2 works fine albeit very slow, and I will stick with it for a
moment.
The Cairo library on my RHEL5 is quite old (1.2.4) but I don't dare to
update it in the middle of the project.

Thank you,

Alex

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: ChromosomeExplorer memory leaks
parts: Hi,

On Mon, Aug 18, 2008 at 7:07 PM, Alex <alex.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
>
> I forced findPngDevice() to return png2: no memory leaks!
that's (kind of) good news.

>
> The default findPngDevice() returned:
> function (...)
> pngTyped(..., bg = NA, type = "cairo")
> <environment: 0x17b59448>
>
> So png2 works fine albeit very slow, and I will stick with it for a
> moment.
> The Cairo library on my RHEL5 is quite old (1.2.4) but I don't dare to
> update it in the middle of the project.

It seems like you have narrowed down the problem with Cairo; both with
the built-in one and with the one in Cairo library. I don't know if
they "link" to the same library, but it would be great if you could do
more troubleshooting outside aroma.affymetrix, e.g. generate a lot of
large PNGs in a for loop and see if you can reproduce it. Then,
update your cairo libs and retry. If you still have problems, report
them to R-devel in order to (i) make others aware of it, and (ii)
maybe someone fix it.

Note, png2() is a wrapper on top of bitmap() which is turn generating
a postscript which is the converted to PNG by an external call to
ghostscript. The latter step is done without waiting for ghostscript
to finish. If you look at running processing on your Linux box (e.g.
'top'), you'll see that there are quite a few ghostscript/gs
processing running. Before Cairo was around I was using png2() to
generate tons of PNG images exactly like this and I never had any
problems, but I though you should be aware of it and if you have too
many arrays/chromosomes you might get too many ghostscript processes
running.

Cheers

Henrik

>
> Alex

Good. No, I haven't observed the problem, but on the other hand it
was a while ago that I processed a large batch of arrays at once, and
then I typically process different arrays on different machines, so
memory leaks kicks in later and I don't recall I paid attention to the
memory for those batches.

So, it might be there on other systems as well. To everyone else, if
you run a large number of arrays, could you please pay attention to
the memory (of your R process) and report back if you see any
suspicious memory usage.

I actually like the postscript-to-PNG generated images because they
are less "bitmappy" than what the original PNG device generated.
However, I know that on some systems ghostscript does a poor job on
fonts and rastering making them look really bad; maybe that is your
case. Ideally you should get the same as what you get if you send it
to a eps/postscript file.

Cheers

Henrik

>> >> >> if (transparent) function(...) png(..., bg=NA) else function(...) png(...);
>>
>> >> >> }
>>
>> >> >> See if you still have memory problems if you set another PNG (or JPG,
>> >> >> ...) device like this. FYI, in R.utils there is also a png2() device
>> >> >> that utilizes the bitmap() device to generate PNGs.
>>
>> >> >> I hope this helps you/us to identify the source of the memory issue,
>> >> >> so we can fix it/work around it. I'm not outruling there is something
>> >> >> funny going on in ChromosomeExplorer et al, but I hope not.
>>
>> >> >> Cheers
>>

messages.subject: Re: ChromosomeExplorer memory leaks
parts:
Hi Henrik,

I modified the plotting functions reducing the line width for regions
to lwd=2 and raw CN pointsize to ces=0.3. Now they look much better.

Best,

Alex

On Aug 19, 2:47 pm, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> Hi.
>

> On Mon, Aug 18, 2008 at 8:36 PM, Alex <alex.lisov...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> > Hi Henrik,
>
> > I'll definetely perform more experiments. But have you experienced the
> > same problem and if yes then on what system(s)? I can use PC or MAC if
> > this problem is specific for 64bit systems. Besides, the png2 graphics
> > looks horrible...
>
> Good.  No, I haven't observed the problem, but on the other hand it
> was a while ago that I processed a large batch of arrays at once, and
> then I typically process different arrays on different machines, so
> memory leaks kicks in later and I don't recall I paid attention to the
> memory for those batches.
>
> So, it might be there on other systems as well.  To everyone else, if
> you run a large number of arrays, could you please pay attention to
> the memory (of your R process) and report back if you see any
> suspicious memory usage.
>
> I actually like the postscript-to-PNG generated images because they
> are less "bitmappy" than what the original PNG device generated.
> However, I know that on some systems ghostscript does a poor job on
> fonts and rastering making them look really bad; maybe that is your
> case.  Ideally you should get the same as what you get if you send it
> to a eps/postscript file.
>
> Cheers
>
> Henrik
>
>
>
> > Thank you,
>
> > Alex
>
> > On Aug 18, 11:15 pm, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu>
> > wrote:
> >> Hi,
>
> >> On Mon, Aug 18, 2008 at 7:07 PM, Alex <alex.lisov...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> >> > Hi Henrik,
>
> >> > I forced findPngDevice() to return png2: no memory leaks!
>
> >> that's (kind of) good news.
>
> >> > The default findPngDevice() returned:
> >> > function (...)
> >> > pngTyped(..., bg = NA, type = "cairo")
> >> > <environment: 0x17b59448>
>
> >> > So png2 works fine albeit very slow, and I will stick with it for a
> >> > moment.
> >> > The Cairo library on my RHEL5 is quite old (1.2.4) but I don't dare to
> >> > update it in the middle of the project.
>
> >> It seems like you have narrowed down the problem with Cairo; both with
> >> the built-in one and with the one in Cairo library.  I don't know if
> >> they "link" to the same library, but it would be great if you could do
> >> more troubleshooting outside aroma.affymetrix, e.g. generate a lot of
> >> large PNGs in a for loop and see if you can reproduce it.  Then,
> >> update your cairo libs and retry.  If you still have problems, report
> >> them to R-devel in order to (i) make others aware of it, and (ii)
> >> maybe someone fix it.
>
> >> Note, png2() is a wrapper on top of bitmap() which is turn generating
> >> a postscript which is the converted to PNG by an external call to
> >> ghostscript.  The latter step is done without waiting for ghostscript
> >> to finish.  If you look at running processing on your Linux box (e.g.
> >> 'top'), you'll see that there are quite a few ghostscript/gs
> >> processing running.  Before Cairo was around I was using png2() to
> >> generate tons of PNG images exactly like this and I never had any
> >> problems, but I though you should be aware of it and if you have too
> >> many arrays/chromosomes you might get too many ghostscript processes
> >> running.
>
> >> Cheers
>
> >> Henrik
>
> >> > Thank you,
>
> >> > Alex
>
> >> > On Aug 18, 5:58 pm, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> >> >> Hi,
>
> >> >> On Mon, Aug 18, 2008 at 2:39 PM, Alex <alex.lisov...@gmail.com> wrote:

>

> >> >> > Here is an example of memory leak report:
> >> >> >http://lists.cairographics.org/archives/cairo-bugs/2008-June/002360.html
>
> >> >> > Googling for "Cairo memory leaks" gives a lot of other links, but I
> >> >> > never worked with Cairo before so I cannot easily determine how close
> >> >> > those reports relate to the problem, at least the link above is
> >> >> > explicitly related.
>
> >> >> > I will try to modify the findPngDevice and report back. Should I

> >> >> >> > On Aug 18, 3:14 pm, "Alex Lisovich" <alex.lisov...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >> >> >> >> Hi All,
>
> >> >> >> >> I am running 250K_Sty analysis of 28 samples against 48 HapMap
> >> >> >> >> reference set. After performing all preprocessing steps I end up with
> >> >> >> >> cesN containing 76 arrays.
>
> >> >> >> >> Next, I do:
>
> >> >> >> >> ces1<-extract(cesN,c(1:28));
> >> >> >> >> ces2<-extract(cesN,c(29:76));
> >> >> >> >> ceRef<-getAverageFile(ces2);
> >> >> >> >> cbs<-CbsModel(ces1,cesRef);
> >> >> >> >> fit(cbs,verbose=verbose);
> >> >> >> >> ce<-ChromosomeExplorer(cbs);
> >> >> >> >> setAlias(ce,"TEST");
>
> >> >> >> >> everything fine at this point. But when I do:
>
> >> >> >> >>  ce<-process(ce,verbose=verbose),
>
> >> >> >> >> the memory consumption grows
> >> >> >> >> steadily from ~2GB to the upper memory limit of 32GB (this happens at the
> >> >> >> >> array# ~ 15) and then the system crashes as expected.
> >> >> >> >> I noticed the previous discussion on this subject in June but looks
> >> >> >> >> like the issue was not resolved.
>
> >> >> >> Could you please give the name of (and URL to) the thread you refer
> >> >> >> to?  If it is the one I guess it is, it should have been solved in the
> >> >> >> latest update.
>
> >> >> >> >>  There is also numerous discussions on
> >> >> >> >> Cairo memory leaks with NVidia (that's what I have) elsewhere, so
> >> >> >> >> probably this is a source of the problem.
> >> >> >> >> Is there a workaround to fight this memory leak or should I generate
> >> >> >> >> reports chunk by chunk of say 10 arrays?
>
> >> >> >> You say above that you have uninstalled Cairo; do you mean the 'Cairo'
> >> >> >> package?  Note that in R there is now a build in cairo device as well,
> >> >> >> which is probably used in your case, because the package tries to
> >> >> >> located a working PNG device in a given order.  Internally, the PNG
> >> >> >> device to be used to generate all graphs is found by:
>
> >> >> >>   pngDev <- findPngDevice(transparent=TRUE);
>
> >> >> >> where findPngDevice() is an internal function located in aroma.core.
> >> >> >> Have a look at the source code for this function in order to see which
> >> >> >> and in what order PNG devices are scanned.
>
> >> >> >> Since we're not using namespaces, you can easily override this
> >> >> >> function to force the use of a specific PNG device, e.g.
>
> >> >> >> findPngDevice <- function(transparent=TRUE, ...) {
> >> >> >>   if (transparent) function(...) png(..., bg=NA) else function(...) png(...);
>
> >> >> >> }
>
> >> >> >> See if you still have memory problems if you set another PNG (or JPG,
> >> >> >> ...) device like this.  FYI, in R.utils there is also a png2() device
> >> >> >> that utilizes the bitmap() device to generate PNGs.
>
> >> >> >> I hope this helps you/us to identify the source of the memory issue,
> >> >> >> so we can fix it/work around it.  I'm not outruling there is something
> >> >> >> funny going on in ChromosomeExplorer et al, but I hope not.
>
> >> >> >> Cheers
>
> >> >> >> Henrik
>
> >> >> >> >> Thank you,
>
